Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA)
Over 40 Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) ratified by Canada, including agreements with major trading partners

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of country of residence; notarized by local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if issued by a Hague Convention party, e.g., China, Hong Kong, Singapore, USA) or Consular Legalization by Canadian consulate for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The corporate registry in the parent corporation's incorporation jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Officer/Director Register (if parent corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The corporate secretary or registered agent of the parent corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with notarization in the country of issue

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for Initial Deposit / Source of Funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Banking institution of the prospective shareholder or director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; in all cases must be notarized within 3 months before submission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the consolidated Canadian Sanctions List (under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act), the OSC/CSA enforcement lists, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) advisory lists, and international references including OFAC SDN, UNSC Consolidated List, and INTERPOL notices. Domestic FINTRAC compliance requires ongoing risk assessment, politically exposed person (PEP) identification for domestic and foreign PEPs, and immediate reporting of any matches to FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (administered by Service Alberta; accessible online through authorized service providers and the official provincial registry portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must use letters of the Latin alphabet; the name may be in English or French, and may include Arabic numerals, hyphens, periods, spaces, and ampersands. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters. The legal element 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Ulc' or 'Company' must be appended as applicable. Statutes require that the name not be likely to confuse and must correspond to the actual business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registry within 30 days of the notice of rejection. The request must include a covering letter, the original rejection notice, and any additional consent letters or evidence of distinguishability. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file a fresh NUANS name search report and re-reserve a new name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the virtual office provider supplies a physical street address in Alberta, during business hours staffed, and where the corporation maintains access to corporate records; a purely postal or mail-forwarding address is not acceptable. The registered office must always be located in Alberta and must serve as the official address for service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – less than 5% per year for an online retail company with no physical storefront; inspection risk rises to 20–30% if the corporation remains non-compliant with annual returns, holds a regulatory approval, or if a formal complaint is received by the Alberta Corporate Registry.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and corporate name reservation
Alberta incorporation filing fee (standard business corporation, no minimum capital)
Registered office address and process service for first year
Preparation of beneficial ownership register and initial UBO disclosure filing (provincial and federal, if applicable)
Notarization and apostille coordination of director and shareholder identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public / Global Affairs Canada consular services (where apostille required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary fee plus government apostille fee (CAD 150)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended (ABCA), particularly sections 2, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12, 15, and 16 governing incorporation, articles, registered office, directors, and officers; no federal incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act is elected.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Registrar of Corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation filed under Part 3 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act, together with the Initial Notice of Registered Office and Directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the ABCA; shares may be issued without par value for nominal or no cash consideration. No escrow account is required; the sole shareholder may capitalize the corporation as needed for operational purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] CORP. (the Corporation), passed on [date], pursuant to the Alberta Business Corporations Act. RESOLVED: (1) The shares set forth in the share subscription schedule are issued to the named subscribers in exchange for lawful consideration; share certificates shall be executed and delivered. (2) The registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [street address, city, province] and the corporate records are established. (3) The following officers are appointed: the President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, with duties prescribed by the Corporation’s bylaws. (4) The directors and officers are authorised to execute all corporate, banking, regulatory, and tax filings necessary to complete the Corporation’s incorporation and commence lawful business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (online through the corporate registry service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request to obtain a NUANS report. Review the name for distinguishability and compliance with ABCA restrictions. If desired, reserve the corporate name for a period of ninety days by submitting the prescribed form and fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or confusing, submit a revised name request with a new NUANS report using distinct elements; the Registry accepts a further application without prejudice after refinements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or duly authorized legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation specifying corporate name, share structure, registered office address, directors, and any special provisions. Prepare the Initial Notice of Registered Office and Directors and obtain consent from each named director.
required_dossiers: Form of Initial Notice of Registered Office and Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requests amendments, revise the relevant fields and resubmit the corrected Articles within the deficiency notice period; no re-notarization is required for ministerial corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation and Initial Notice through the authorized electronic filing channel. Pay the statutory filing fee. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Initial Notice of Registered Office and Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, the Registry sends a deficiency notice. Curing is achieved by correcting the stated defect and resubmitting or by responding to the Registrar’s written request within the specified period; service is expedited after completion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office Address (non-residential location in Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office address and open the corporation books; update the corporate minute book with the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, Bylaws, resolutions, and registers maintaining shareholder and director records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is later invalidated, file a Notice of Change of Registered Office with the Registry and revise the corporate minute book to maintain statutory compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Federal and Alberta Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (for applicable provincial programs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal Business Number (BN) and register for Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST). Register for Alberta corporate income tax account with CRA; obtain import/export and program accounts only if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA flags the application, provide clarifying documents through the Business Account portal or call the Registered Client Sign-In; resolution generally occurs within service standard timelines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Municipal Authorizations for E-Commerce Retail
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Licencing Department (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton as applicable); Alberta occupational and fire safety authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal general retail business licence for the principal place of business or warehouse. Secure any applicable home occupation licence if operations are conducted from a residential address. Verify compliance with Alberta OHS and fire codes for storage and shipping of portable battery products.
required_dossiers: Temporary Storage Permit (if applicable for lithium-battery inventory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires additional documentation, respond to the written deficiency list within 30 days; a temporary licence may be issued pending full compliance under Alberta's Municipal Government Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licencing Department of the local municipality (e.g., City of Calgary Licensing Authority or City of Edmonton Permits and Licensing Authority)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Retail Business Licence (and Home Occupation Business Licence, if applicable)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA registration required for e-commerce retail warehousing; only compliance with solid and hazardous waste management rules for battery products is applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge from retail operations; ventilation and indoor air quality for small-scale warehouse space must meet Alberta occupational exposure limits; discarded lithium batteries must be segregated and shipped to a licensed recycling facility, with no subsurface disposal or uncontrolled incineration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code for the warehouse or storage area; structural load approval for shelving and storage racks; municipal building and occupancy clearance; workplace health and safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code for material handling and hazardous goods.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); GST/HST and corporate tax registration administered through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services.html). Alberta corporate income tax is also administered by CRA under the Alberta Tax Administration Agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Canadian corporations must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA and activate Program Accounts for GST/HST (RT), Corporate Income Tax (RC), and Payroll (RP) if applicable. Registration is completed online via BRO or by mail using Form RC1. No minimum capital, notarization, or local director requirement applies for a federally or provincially incorporated subsidiary. The GST/HST account must be opened before the first taxable supply is made; non-resident directors must file prescribed contact information with CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Canadian corporation is a taxable entity subject to federal corporate income tax at 15% and Alberta provincial corporate income tax at 8% (combined 23% on Alberta-allocated income). Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on a pass-through basis, and Canadian-resident subsidiaries are not eligible for transparent classification for Canadian tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada; a Canadian incorporated corporation is a per-se taxable entity. Available elections include: GST/HST Quick Method election for small suppliers (Excise Tax Act section 227), election to treat taxable supplies between closely related corporations as non-taxable (Excise Tax Act section 156), Canadian-controlled private corporation capital dividend account election, and specified election under Income Tax Act section 216 for net rental income. Hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act sections 18.4 to 18.7 limit inappropriate deduction/non-inclusion outcomes. Fiscal consolidation is not permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – Federal value-added tax; Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) does not apply in Alberta. Alberta imposes no provincial retail sales tax or provincial branch of the GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 per calendar quarter (small supplier threshold) for domestic and non-resident suppliers. Under digital economy measures effective July 1, 2021, non-resident sellers and distribution platform operators making taxable supplies of digital or tangible personal property to Canadian consumers must register once total taxable worldwide supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any calendar quarter or trailing 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime in Alberta or federally. CRA accepts electronic records and e-invoices; PEPPOL BIS 3.0 interchange is voluntary. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis depending on taxable supplies. Distribution platform operators are deemed registrants for non-resident third-party sellers and must maintain transaction-level data and remit GST/HST on supplies facilitated through their platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported tangible personal property is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act provided the supplier retains documentary proof of export within 60 days of the sale and property is exported by the supplier, purchaser, or an authorized agent. Portable solar generators and solar panels sold to non-residents for delivery outside Canada qualify for 0% GST. Services rendered to non-residents are generally zero-rated when the service is not performed in Canada or is performed in Canada but exclusively for a non-resident client. Domestic sales to Canadian consumers in Alberta remain taxable at 5% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Canada Customs Export Declaration (or approved alternative for low-value postal/express shipments)
Commercial invoice showing buyer identity, destination address, and HS classification (HS 8501.61, 8501.31, 8541.43)
Bill of Lading / cargo control document (A8A) or courier air waybill
Foreign delivery proof (courier tracking history, customs clearance record at destination)
Inward remittance certificate or cross-border payment record evidencing foreign exchange settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA verifies zero-rating claims under Excise Tax Act sections 221(1) and 223. Failure to substantiate exports results in reassessment of GST at 5%, denial of related input tax credits, and interest under section 280. Gross negligence penalties of 25% of the tax sought to be evaded apply for false statements; full-assessment penalties range from 5% to 10% plus aggregate interest. Fraudulent export zero-rating is criminally prosecutable under Excise Tax Act section 332 and Income Tax Act section 239, with fines up to CAD 20,000 and imprisonment for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency regime. Current account transactions are freely convertible without restriction or prior approval. Capital account transactions by Canadian corporations, including profit remittances, dividends, and capital contributions, are generally permitted without regulatory approval provided they comply with tax filing obligations under the Income Tax Act and reporting requirements under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. No prior approval is required for routine remittances; however, transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 may trigger enhanced scrutiny and beneficial ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canadian exporters are not subject to mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Repatriation to Canada is encouraged but not statutorily mandated within a fixed timeline. Proceeds must be reported to authorized foreign exchange dealers, with all foreign exchange transactions conducted only through licensed dealers. No mandatory conversion ratios apply; market rates govern all transactions. Companies must maintain records for audit purposes and comply with FINTRAC reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions and cross-border payment platforms such as Wise or equivalent regulated providers are viable for Canadian corporations subject to full compliance with Canadian anti-money laundering standards, FATCA and CRS reporting, and FINTRAC registration requirements. Legal constraints include mandatory use of licensed payment service providers, prohibition on unlicensed offshore issuance of electronic money, and potential restrictions on anonymity features. Offshore digital EMIs must obtain proper Canadian regulatory approvals or partner with federally regulated entities to avoid violations of the Payment Services Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding with video KYC verification is permitted for most Tier 1 Canadian banks for Alberta-based corporations. Directors and authorized signers may complete onboarding electronically using government-issued ID verification and video interviews. In-person appearance is required only for higher-risk accounts, large transaction volumes, or when enhanced due diligence is triggered; otherwise, remote video conferencing satisfies regulatory standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent beneficial ownership information or undisclosed controlling persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extract, shareholder register, beneficial ownership declaration, corporate resolution authorizing account opening, and source of funds documentation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving high-risk jurisdictions or politically exposed persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file including source of wealth evidence, independent business verification, senior management approval, and transaction purpose justification

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from foreign shareholders or investors are routed via international SWIFT wire transfers to the Canadian corporate operating account. Required purpose codes include 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. All transactions require full KYC/AML verification, beneficial ownership disclosure, corporate resolution, and source of funds documentation. Large or unusual inflows must be reported to FINTRAC within prescribed timelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for goods purchases are settled using SWIFT MT103 messages or issuance of commercial letters of credit through Canadian banks. Standard purpose code is 'Payment for Goods/Services'. Commercial LCs are permissible for larger transactions with full trade documentation including purchase orders, invoices, and shipping documents. All settlements must comply with export/import licensing where applicable and be recorded for tax and audit purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within two months after each anniversary date of incorporation or registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in registry enforcement and additional service or reinstatement charges. The Registrar may dissolve the corporation after statutory notice and failure to remedy the default; no fixed statutory late-filing penalty or universal strike-off interval applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporations Canada Annual Return, if federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in compliance notices, monetary penalties for specified offences, and administrative dissolution after the statutory default and notice process. Restoration may require filing outstanding returns and paying applicable fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File with the annual return and promptly after changes to registered office, directors, or corporate information.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or outdated registry information may result in compliance action, penalties under applicable corporate legislation, and inability to complete certain registry transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Individual Significant Control Register Review, if federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada upon statutory request; not ordinarily filed as an annual public return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Review at least annually and update the register within 15 days after becoming aware of a change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or produce the register may expose the corporation and responsible individuals to offences, fines, and compliance orders under the Canada Business Corporations Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For an Alberta private corporation, there is generally no revenue, asset, or employee threshold that independently triggers an audit. An auditor is generally required unless shareholders validly waive the appointment by the required unanimous shareholder resolution. Publicly accountable or securities-reporting entities may not use the private-company exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for an eligible private corporation; IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises and may be adopted where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An Alberta corporation should maintain current records identifying registered shareholders, beneficial owners, control relationships, and transfers, and confirm them during the annual corporate review. Alberta does not generally require a separate annual public UBO filing. A federally incorporated corporation must maintain an Individual Significant Control register, review it at least annually, and update it within 15 days of a change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Individual Significant Control Register, if federally incorporated

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500-5,000 for a small private ecommerce corporation; higher where inventory, payment-platform reconciliation, foreign transactions, or complex revenue recognition is involved

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 38% federal general corporate income tax rate; 15% small business rate on first $500,000 of taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction, SR&ED tax credits (refundable up to 100%), accelerated capital cost allowance (CCA) claims

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically via CRA My Business Account portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end date (June 15 for calendar year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from all sources including sales of goods and services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only Canadian-source income; worldwide income if carrying on business in Canada

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after allowable deductions and losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents limited to Canadian-source income; foreign tax credits claimed where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income for tax purposes before adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents apply same rules but restrict to Canadian-source net income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated tax after applicable rates and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute tax on Canadian-source income only

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 5% of tax payable per month, maximum 12 months; 1% per month interest on unpaid tax after 30 days

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 to CRA with supporting tax treaty documentation, beneficial ownership certificate, and residency proof to claim reduced treaty rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 25% federal statutory rate; Royalties: 25% federal statutory rate; reduced under applicable tax treaties (e.g., 0% US, 10% UK, 15% OECD model)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for related-party transactions requiring local file transfer pricing documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a comprehensive Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; compliance governed by Income Tax Act transfer pricing rules, General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), and substance-over-form principles

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of T2 return by statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 5% penalty of tax payable per month up to 12 months plus interest on unpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited personal liability; willful non-compliance may expose directors to criminal charges and director liability provisions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Understatement of income or false statements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misrepresentation of revenue, expenses, or related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to 50% of tax evaded, plus interest and potential reassessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal penalties and, in cases of willful evasion, criminal prosecution with imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation or use non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjustments to transfer prices, penalties up to 10% of transaction value, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Potential personal liability for willful transfer pricing violations under Income Tax Act

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold and remit 25% WHT on dividends to non-resident shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to the withheld tax plus interest; possible director liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid WHT in certain circumstances; potential criminal sanctions for evasion
